concept.name: Inverse head and shoulders
concept.definition: The bullish mirror of the head-and-shoulders top: three successive troughs after a downtrend in which the middle trough (the head) is the deepest and the two outside troughs (the shoulders) are shallower, with the intervening reaction highs forming a neckline. The pattern is treated as complete only when price breaks above the neckline, ideally with a clear volume expansion, marking a tentative bullish reversal. Like all chart patterns it is a heuristic framework, not a proven predictive law.
concept.intuition: Sellers drive price to a final capitulation low (the head), but the next decline (the right shoulder) cannot reach it — supply is drying up. A break above neckline resistance shows buyers have seized control.
concept.mechanics: Identify an established downtrend, then three troughs with the middle one deepest; draw the neckline through the two reaction highs. Confirmation requires a convincing close above the neckline; volume plays a larger role than in the top version — expanding volume on the advance and breakout is considered close to mandatory. The price target projects the head-to-neckline distance upward from the break.
concept.formula: Price target = N + (N - H), where H = price at the bottom of the head and N = neckline price at the breakout point.
concept.failure_modes: Fails when price stalls at the neckline and the downtrend resumes, or when a low-volume breakout quickly fails and price falls back below the right-shoulder low. Because bottoms form slowly, the pattern is frequently 'called' long before it is complete.
concept.misconceptions: That three troughs alone confirm a bottom — the pattern is incomplete until neckline resistance breaks with volume. Perfect shoulder symmetry is often demanded but is explicitly not required.
concept.example: A stock declines to $50 (left shoulder), capitulates to $48 (head), rebounds to $61, then dips only to $57 (right shoulder). A high-volume close above the $61 neckline completes the pattern with a measured target near $74.

citations.source: StockCharts ChartSchool: Head and Shoulders Bottom
Lo, Mamaysky & Wang, 'Foundations of Technical Analysis' (NBER Working Paper 7613)
